/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 14 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2980 (20)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4751 (49)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2251 (1)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1710 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 909 (-5)
CAPESIZE
The market edged higher today, with the BCI 5TC increasing by $445 to settle at $43,086. While the overall index extended its recent run of gains, the advance was modest, with strength in the Atlantic offsetting a quieter Pacific session. In the Pacific, activity eased slightly after yesterday’s late flurry of fixtures, although the market remained steady. All three major miners were active on C5, with one fixing at $13.25 before another concluded at $13.30. Owners’ ideas were generally reported in the mid to upper $13s, reflecting firmer sentiment despite the C5 index easing marginally by 0.065 to $13.420. The Atlantic basin continued to firm, providing the main support for today’s index gain. Conditions on the South Brazil and West Africa to China route improved further, with offers for early August loading reported around $35.00, while end-August dates attracted a slight discount. A reported fixture at $34.85 for 8–12 August loading helped establish market levels, with the C3 index climbing $1.495 to $34.605.
PANAMAX
The North Atlantic still seems to be waiting for something to happen and both routes dropped slightly today. The clear out seen last week seems to have more ships being replenished so far, although Owners are generally continuing to hold their offers. In the South, after a slow start yesterday, there seemed to be some fixing at improved levels from EC South America during the middle of the day with talk of a few vessels obtaining the equivalent of $21,000 on P6, although we wait to hear details on these fixtures. In Asia there were small gains again today, although the market looks generally balanced as it has done for some time now. The Shandong Fu You (81,782 2018) Longkou 15-17 July fixed for about 3 months trading redelivery worldwide at 104% of the 5TC average to Ultimar, whilst there were more Indonesian coal fixtures still emerging with the Xinde Fortune (82,688 2007) Hong Kong 12-14 July fixed via Indonesia to India to undisclosed Charterers. The 5TC average was up slightly to $20,260, an increase of just $6.
SUPRAMAX
More activity today, albeit mostly catching up and reporting of fixtures from last week, of which there seemed to be many. The North Americas were marked down slightly by brokers with some commenting the momentum seems to have eased. Across the Atlantic the East Mediterranean still looked tight for tonnage whilst West Africa was experiencing delays which appeared to benefit the few who found themselves on the right dates at the right time. In Asia there were negligible gains again today, which can be seen as a positive given the balanced nature of the present market. The Ocean Ace (55,697 2005) CJK 19-25 July was fixed via China with intention steels redelivery Thailand in the mid $16,000’s and an Ultramax was said to have fixed aps Samalaju for a trip to the US Gulf again intention steels at around $15,000, but there were no further details on either. The 11TC average saw a small gain of $46 to close the day at $21,619.
HANDYSIZE
It was a day of mixed activity with only slight fluctuations observed across both basins. The BHSI edged down by 5 points to 909, while the 7TC average fell by $75 closing at $16,370. In the Continent and Mediterranean fresh demand and increased activity were reported, with rates reflecting a slightly firmer tone. Meanwhile the South Atlantic and US Gulf continued to soften, as demand remained insufficient to absorb the growing tonnage list. On the fixture side, the Indonesia Bulker (37,725 2017) was placed on subjects for a trip delivery Houston to Santo Tomas at $20,500 by Pangaea but other details were not disclosed. Across Asia the market held largely steady with both the tonnage list and cargo availability showing little change in the main loading regions. A 28,000-dwt open Thailand fixed to South China at $10,000 though further details remain undisclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Coal Imports

Chinese coal imports rose 9.5 Mt from May, and 9.7 Mt year-on-year to 42.8 Mt in June, the highest monthly volume since January, preliminary customs data show. In the first half of the year, total coal imports stood 3.7 Mt higher at 225.4 Mt.

According to McCloskey, May’s fatal mine accident in Shanxi interrupted production in domestic thermal and coking coal mines with widespread safety inspections. Combined with high temperature expectations linked to El Niño before peak summer demand season, traders and power generators pushed to frontload coal stocks.
Sent from Front

Trading Commentary
Cape
A tale of two halves for Cape FFA, starting strong out of the blocks with Jul and Aug paid highs of 37250 and 36000 respectively. Despite another positive physical index print of +445, the afternoon session hosted a series of better offers, leaving the curve closing in the red for the day. Jul traded down to lows of 36250, closing at 36400 for the day. Aug traded down to 34750, and closing just off that level. Sep traded 36750-35800, closing at 36000. Q4 traded up to highs of 35750, before closing down $300 at 35300. Cal27 traded 28900-28750. C28 traded a few times between 25000-24900.

PMX
The pmx market traded flat in the morning, losing support later in the day. July traded between 19,850–20,500, with early strength to 20,500 before easing back to 20,200 into the close. August dominated the front, trading in a 19,550–20,100 range. After reaching 20,100 early. September traded between 19,850–20,450, peaking early before settling around 20,100 late. Q3 26 traded at 20,100–20,250, while Q4 26 saw the most interest, printing between 19,500–19,850. Cal 27 traded actively from 16,400–16,600, while Cal 28 had a single print at 14,700.

SMX + HANDY
July traded between 19,350–19,450. August was the most active contract, dealing from 19,300 down to 19,000. September traded between 18,850–19,100, with late activity centred around 18,900. Q3 26 moved from 19,300 early to 19,000 later in the day, while Q4 26 printed around 18,200. Further along the curve, Q1 27 lowered to 13,850, while Cal 27 traded at 14,450 seeing a single print lower at 14,300.

ai_analysis.summary: 2026年7月14日波罗的海干散货指数整体上扬，BDI上涨20点至2980，录得连续升势；海岬型领涨BCI升49点，但远期曲线走弱显示市场对短期上方空间存疑；巴拿马型和超灵便型稳中有升，灵便型小幅回落。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 干散货市场整体趋强，BCI 5TC升至43086美元日涨445，大西洋航线特别是巴西和西非至中国表现亮眼，C3跳涨1.495至34.605；太平洋C5略显疲态降0.065至13.42；巴拿马型及超灵便型维持区间震荡，灵便型回落5点。远期曲线呈近弱远稳格局，7-9月合约普遍下跌150-450点。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 看涨信号：C3航线持续反弹，大西洋可用运力趋紧推升费率；超灵便型11TC维持涨势。看跌信号：FFA曲线前端走弱，7月海岬型合约大跌300-450；灵便型7TC回落75美元；太平洋航线成交放缓。整体信号偏中性偏多，关注C3能否突破35美元阻力位。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 海岬型：近月合约承压，C3航线可逢低做多，关注8月装港机会；巴拿马型：5TC维持窄幅整理，关注南美谷物出口季启动；超灵便型：亚洲印尼煤航线保持活跃，费率相对坚挺；套利：Q4海岬型合约贴水结构提供跨期机会。

market_watch: C3航线（巴西至中国）突破35美元将确认大西洋强势延续
FFA曲线海岬型前端走弱是否预示现货上行动能衰减
灵便型持续走弱是否会拖累整体干散货市场情绪

route_focus.view: 大西洋支撑强劲，C3升1.495至34.605，早8月装港报价约35美元，短期有望测试35美元关口，建议关注运费衍生品做多机会。
泛太平洋航线维持平衡，5TC报20260微升6美元，印尼煤出口稳定但上方空间有限，预计短期维持19800-20500区间震荡。
灵便型偏弱，Skaw-Passero至Rio航线报8236涨79，但整体7TC跌75至16370，大西洋运力过剩压制费率反弹空间。
